meta.scenario: UI/UX follow-state desynchronization between frontend optimistic update, Flask API, PostgreSQL followers table, and Redis cache
meta.purpose: Provide faulty inputs and reproduction evidence for an AI agent to diagnose and fix inconsistent follow/unfollow UI states.

notes: followers table does NOT have tenant_id column
Redis keys do NOT include tenant_id
follow_status API reads Redis first, does NOT reconcile with DB when cache is stale
UI flips button state BEFORE HTTP 200 is received

followers_table.ddl: CREATE TABLE followers (follower_id INTEGER NOT NULL, followed_id INTEGER NOT NULL);

faulty_models.user_model_snippet:
class User(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    tenant_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)
    # ... other fields ...

test_cases.description: UI shows 'Following' immediately, but refresh reads stale Redis which still says not-following.
actual_events: frontend -> page reload -> GET /follow_status/202 -> returns {"following": false}
test_cases.observed_bug: After reload UI returns to 'Follow' even though DB already has row.

test_cases.description: Rapid follow/unfollow from the same user leads to nondeterministic final UI state because cache writes are not atomic.
actual_events: DB final state: follower row EXISTS
test_cases.observed_bug: DB and Redis diverge; UI renders the wrong one.

test_cases.description: Because Redis keys are missing tenant scoping, tenant 2 reads tenant 1's follow state.
actual_events: tenant 1 user 5001 follows 5002 -> Redis set follow_status:5001:5002=1
tenant 2 user with same numeric ids queries /follow_status -> returns 1
tenant 2 UI shows 'Following' even though no relationship in tenant 2 DB
test_cases.observed_bug: shared Redis keyspace leaks follow state across tenants.

test_cases.description: Soft-deleted follower rows are still reported as active in Redis.
actual_events: DB: followers row marked deleted = true
test_cases.observed_bug: UI shows following for a soft-deleted relationship because cache was never invalidated.

test_cases.description: Frontend commits to 'Following' without waiting for HTTP 200; backend actually failed (IntegrityError) but UI never rolled back.
actual_events: backend: 500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR (IntegrityError: duplicate key)
test_cases.observed_bug: UI permanently shows 'Following' even though backend failed.

flask_app.log: INFO 2025-11-10T11:58:01Z SQL INSERT INTO followers (follower_id, followed_id) VALUES (101,202);

expected_agent_actions: add tenant_id to followers table and to Redis key structure
modify /follow_status to reconcile Redis and DB when mismatch detected
change frontend follow button to wait for HTTP 200 before committing to 'Following'
add tests to simulate cache delay and concurrent toggle
produce output.json summarizing root causes, fixes, and test results
